answer: Each agent deposits a unique cryptographic token forged from a hash of a secret phrase that includes a seasonal word like pearl and a random basalt‑derived nonce, then publishes only the hash. In the reveal phase agents disclose the full phrase; the network verifies the hash and checks that the phrase was not previously recorded in any garden ledger, rejecting duplicates. An attacker must generate distinct, verifiable phrases for every fake identity, incurring linear computational and storage costs proportional to the number of Sybil nodes.
